central_figure.name: Mark Carney
central_figure.role: PM 2025-present / Brookfield Vice-Chair 2020-2024 / UN Climate Envoy 2020+ / BoE Governor 2013-2020 / Bank of Canada Governor 2008-2013
central_figure.notable: Unique cross-sector trajectory: Bank of Canada Governor (2008-2013) through the 2008 financial crisis, Bank of England Governor (2013-2020), joined Brookfield Asset Management as Vice-Chair and Head of Transition Investing (August 2020) concurrently with UN Special Envoy for Climate Action and Finance appointment (November 2020). Reported to hold substantial Brookfield stock options (~C$6.8M disclosed). Became Trudeau's informal economic advisor 2024, Liberal leader and PM March 2025.

brookfield_corporate.name: Bruce Flatt
brookfield_corporate.notable: 23-year CEO of Brookfield. Oversaw growth from C$10B AUM to over C$1T by 2024. Directly hired Carney as Vice-Chair in August 2020. Continues to lead the firm Carney was Vice-Chair of.

brookfield_corporate.name: Brookfield Asset Management
brookfield_corporate.notable: Global alternative-asset manager headquartered in Toronto. AUM exceeds C$1T as of 2024 — larger than the Canadian federal budget. Portfolio includes infrastructure, renewables, private equity, credit, real estate. Benefits materially from Canadian federal policy on climate transition, infrastructure, and real-estate regulation — all areas where Carney held simultaneous UN Climate Envoy and Brookfield Vice-Chair roles 2020-2024.

brookfield_corporate.name: Brookfield Renewable Partners
brookfield_corporate.notable: The Brookfield subsidiary positioned to benefit directly from Canadian federal climate-transition grants, green-bonds framework, and carbon-pricing architecture. Carney's 2020-2024 role as Head of Transition Investing at Brookfield was explicitly about directing climate-aligned capital into assets Brookfield Renewable holds.

finance_ministers.name: Bill Morneau
finance_ministers.notable: Finance Minister through the 2015-2020 Trudeau first and second terms. Resigned August 2020 over the WE Charity affair — found to have accepted trips paid by WE with related-party conflict. Paid $50K penalty to Ethics Commissioner in 2023 to avoid censure. Family Morneau Shepell pension-consulting firm held extensive federal contracts during his tenure.

finance_ministers.name: Chrystia Freeland
finance_ministers.notable: Four-year Finance Minister. Tabled budgets containing climate-transition grants and green-bonds framework that materially benefited Brookfield Renewable. Family wealth and Ukrainian business interests disclosed. Resigned from cabinet December 2024 over disagreement with Trudeau on fiscal policy, hours before a fiscal update.

finance_ministers.name: Dominic LeBlanc
finance_ministers.notable: Briefly held Finance portfolio December 2024 – March 2025 during Trudeau's final months. Already cross-axis in corrections and foreign-interference dossiers.

finance_ministers.name: Francois-Philippe Champagne
finance_ministers.notable: Current Finance Minister under PM Carney. Previously FA 2019-2021 (arms pipeline cross-axis). Responsible for any Brookfield-adjacent fiscal decisions in the Carney government.

bank_of_canada_governors.name: Stephen Poloz
bank_of_canada_governors.notable: Carney-appointed Senior Deputy (2013) who succeeded him as Governor when Carney left for the Bank of England. Seven-year term through the 2015-2020 Liberal fiscal expansion.

bank_of_canada_governors.name: Tiff Macklem
bank_of_canada_governors.notable: Current Bank of Canada Governor. Term includes COVID-era quantitative easing, post-pandemic inflation, and the monetary policy context for Brookfield's infrastructure and real-estate holdings. Overlapping Brookfield relationship documented in his previous private-sector roles.

financial_regulators.name: Sarah Paquet
financial_regulators.role: Director, Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
financial_regulators.notable: Director of Canada's anti-money-laundering agency since 2020. FINTRAC's budget has been held roughly flat in real dollars over a period of documented rapid growth in Canadian money-laundering volume (Cullen Commission found $5B+ annually laundered through BC real estate alone, 2022). The budget-vs-mandate gap is a documented capture signal for the Carney-adjacent financial architecture.

financial_regulators.name: Peter Routledge
financial_regulators.notable: OSFI Superintendent since 2021. Regulates banks, insurers, and pension plans — including the pension plans Brookfield manages. Previous role: Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation CEO.

senior_finance_bureaucrats.name: Michael Sabia
senior_finance_bureaucrats.notable: Deputy Minister of Finance 2020-2023 — the top bureaucrat in the department through Morneau's resignation, the Freeland era, and the design of the climate-transition grant architecture that benefits Brookfield Renewable. Previous role: CEO of Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec (CDPQ) 2009-2020, one of Canada's largest pension funds — a direct peer institution to Brookfield in the Canadian alternative-asset space. Returned to senior advisory role for PM Carney 2025.

ethics_commissioners.name: Mary Dawson
ethics_commissioners.role: Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner
ethics_commissioners.notable: Ten-year Ethics Commissioner. Oversaw the early Trudeau-era conflict files including Trudeau's Bahamas trip. Found Trudeau in violation of the Conflict of Interest Act four times.

ethics_commissioners.name: Mario Dion
ethics_commissioners.role: Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner
ethics_commissioners.notable: Ethics Commissioner through the WE Charity (Trudeau Report), SNC-Lavalin (Trudeau II Report) findings. Retired 2023. His successor's investigation of Carney-Brookfield matters remains an outstanding accountability question.

ethics_commissioners.name: Konrad von Finckenstein
ethics_commissioners.role: Interim Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner
ethics_commissioners.notable: Retired judge who served as interim Commissioner. Tenure covered the Carney-transition-to-PM period in which any Brookfield-related conflict ruling would have been politically consequential.

timeline.event: Mark Carney appointed Bank of Canada Governor at age 43.
Carney departs BoC for Bank of England. Poloz succeeds him.
Trudeau sworn in. Morneau appointed Finance Minister.
Ethics Commissioner Dawson rules Trudeau violated Conflict of Interest Act — Aga Khan trip.
WE Charity affair surfaces. Morneau acknowledges undisclosed WE-paid travel.
Carney joins Brookfield Asset Management as Vice-Chair and Head of Transition Investing.
UN Special Envoy for Climate Action and Finance role formally announced for Carney.
Cullen Commission Final Report: $5B+ annually laundered through BC alone; FINTRAC budget flat.
Morneau pays $50K penalty to avoid Ethics Commissioner censure over WE.
Mario Dion retires as Ethics Commissioner. Konrad von Finckenstein appointed interim.
Freeland budget 2024 contains climate-transition grants and green-bond framework benefitting Brookfield Renewable.
Freeland resigns as Finance Min hours before fall fiscal update.
Trudeau announces intent to resign as Liberal leader. Carney signals leadership run.
Carney wins Liberal leadership. Sworn in as PM 14 March.
Liberals win election under Carney. Champagne appointed Finance Minister.

statutory_framework: Conflict of Interest Act — S.C. 2006, c. 9, s. 2
Parliament of Canada Act — R.S.C. 1985, c. P-1
Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act — S.C. 2000, c. 17 (governs FINTRAC)
Bank of Canada Act — R.S.C. 1985, c. B-2
oversight_bodies: Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner (operates under the COIA)
oversight_body_limits: Ethics Commissioner can investigate but cannot compel; rulings only
FINTRAC budget has not kept pace with documented money-laundering growth
judicial_instruments_invoked: Cullen Commission — BC money laundering (2019-2022, Final Report June 2022)
accountability_chain.result_2025: Carney is PM. Brookfield Asset Management manages over C$1T. Morneau paid $50K and avoided formal Ethics censure. No Canadian office-holder has been charged with a financial-conflict offence despite documented conflicts.
